messages.content: You are an expert competitive programmer. Produce a correct and efficient Python solution.

Solve this competitive programming problem in Python 3.10. Return the complete solution in one ```python``` block. Problem: Read problem statements in [Mandarin], [Bengali], [Russian], and [Vietnamese] as well. In addition to Competitive Programming, Chef recently developed an interest in Web Dev and started learning HTML. Now he wants to create his own HTML Code Editor. As a subproblem, he wants to check if a typed HTML closing tag has correct syntax or not. A closing HTML tag must: Start with "" Have only lower-case alpha-numeric characters as its body (between ""). That is, each character of the body should either be a digit or a lower-case English letter. Have a non-empty body. Help Chef by printing "Success" if the tag is fine. If not, print "Error". ------ Input Format ------ - The first line contains an integer T, the number of test cases. Then T test cases follow. - Each test case is a single line of input, a string describing the tag. ------ Output Format ------ For each test case, output in a single line, "Success" if it is a valid closing tag and "Error" otherwise (without quotes). You may print each character of the string in uppercase or lowercase (for example, the strings "SuccEss", "success", "Success", "SUCCESS" etc. will all be treated as identical). ------ Constraints ------ $1 ≤ T ≤ 1000$ $1 ≤$ $\mathrm{length}(\mathrm{Tag})$ $≤ 1000$ - The characters of the string belong to the ASCII range $[33, 126]$ (note that this excludes space.) ----- Sample Input 1 ------ 5 Clearly_{Invalid} ----- Sample Output 1 ------ Success Error Success Success Error ----- explanation 1 ------ Test Cases $1, 3, 4$: The tags follow all mentioned constraints. Test Case $2$: The tag doesn't contain opening and closing symbols and also includes characters other than lower-case alpha-numeric characters in its body. Test Case $5$: The tag also includes an upper-case alpha-numeric character "A" and a non alpha-numeric character "/" in its body. Write a complete program that reads standard input and prints the required output. Think carefully about correctness, edge cases and time/memory complexity. Previous candidate: ```python import sys def is_valid_tag(tag: bytes) -> bool: # Minimum valid tag is if len(tag) < 4: return False if not tag.startswith(b''): return False body = tag[2:-1] if len(body) == 0: return False for ch in body: if not (97 <= ch <= 122 or 48 <= ch <= 57): # a-z or 0-9 return False return True def main() -> None: data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split() if not data: return t = int(data[0]) answers = [] for i in range(1, t + 1): tag = data[i] answers.append("Success" if is_valid_tag(tag) else "Error") sys.stdout.write("\n".join(answers)) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Verifier feedback: Wrong answer. Fix the solution and return the corrected complete Python program/function.
